question: Does bf2.8's cost model (half the BrightFunded MT5 spread snapshot of 2026-10-21, median of 10 samples, + 1.2 bp commission per side) match the spreads actually quoted at the times the book trades?
data: research_data/firm_ticks/BrightFunded_Ltd (MT5 COPY_TICKS_INFO, 2026-10-04..2026-11-04; server timestamps verified = UTC by matching BTC mid to Binance 1-minute closes: corr 0.987 at offset 0 h); BTC / ETH full days, other crypto CFDs and indices 23:00-02:00 UTC only

method.spread: per tick (ask - bid) / mid in bp; per day and window the median
method.trade window: hh:05-hh:15 UTC (the MT5 bridge runs about 10 minutes after the hourly book)
method.per coin / hour: median over days of the window medians; weekday and weekend separately
method.hours without ticks (altcoins outside 23: the coin's median over its 23:00-02:00 windows excluding 23:55-00:15 ('normal' level)
method.cost impact: rebuild bf2.8's net positions exactly as CN-2; per coin and hour cost = half the tick spread + 1.2 bp; book Sharpe 2022-26 with the CN-2 netted cost replaced by the tick-based netted cost; index CFDs unchanged (1 bp per side)

descriptive extras (no adoption): spread in 00:15-00:25 / 00:30-00:40 / 01:05-01:15 windows for the 00:00 UTC rebalance (would a later rebalance be cheaper?); any change of the rebalance time needs its own protocol
decision: tick-based Sharpe within 0.03 of CN-2's 3.149: the cost model stands. Lower by more: the CFD planning level is cut by the difference and the measured per-coin spreads replace the snapshot in the live cost tables (a coin whose 00:00 spread exceeds 50 bp is flagged for the exclusion rule). Higher: no change to planning (one month of ticks, conservative side).
